caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 45 of 2004
lawyer:
Syed Ziaul Karim, Advocate, instructed by Md Nowab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Not represented—The Respondent-State.
parties:
Abul Hashem ------ Petitioner
Vs.
State represented by the DC, Cox''s Bazar ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J: Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 10-1-2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1250 of 1996 discharging the Rule, the petitioner Abul Hashem, seeks leave to appeal. 

 2. The aforesaid petitioner was implicated in Chokoria Police Station Case No. 6 dated 7-9-1995 under section 5 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance. Under the provision of aforesaid Ordinance, the Special Tribunal constituted under the Special Powers Act, 1974 took cognisance of the offence, to try the case. 

 4. Mr Syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, referring to section 29 of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishes Bidhan) Ain, 1995, hereinafter referred to as the Act, submits that under the aforesaid provision of law, the case against the petitioner cannot be tried by the Special Tribunal under the Ordinance in view of repeal of the said Ordinance on 17-7-1995 and, as such, according to the learned Advocate, the High Court Division committed error in not quashing the proceeding. 

 5. On perusal of the aforesaid provision of law it appears that the cases in which First Information Reports have been submitted or charge-sheets have been filed before repeal of the Ordinance, could be tried under the repealed Ordinance. But, it appears that in the instant case the First Information Report was lodged on 7-9-1995, and the Police report (charge-sheet) has been submitted on 12-12-1995 i.e. after 17-7-1995 the date of repeal and, as such, this case is required to be tried under the provision of the Act and not under the provision of the old repealed Ordinance. The learned Advocate of the petitioner, however, is candid enough as to concede that the case, in such circumstance, is triable under the Act of 1995. 

 6. In this view of the above admitted position and in order to avoid delay in disposal of the case, we are led to opine that ends of justice would be met if the petition is disposed of without granting leave. In the premises we direct that the accused petitioner is required to be tried under the provision of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishes Bidhan) Ain, 1995 and not under the provision of repealed law i.e. the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983. The Court below is directed to take steps for holding the trial of the case under the provisions of Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishes Bidhan) Ain, 1995 in the light of the observation/direction made above.
